nodes.title: State file kept in canonical form by every service write
nodes.outcome: The service writes orchestration/state.json in canonical form on every write, the cost record included, so `plan-state check` reports no invariant-1 warning.
nodes.note: Raised by the reviewer of P4-N049 (T190) as D106. Writes to majodali/project-orchestrator-service, where the owner merges and a merge deploys; a pin move in this repository follows. Repository: that one and this one. This node's plan needs no file (D108): docs/plans/rebuild.md stands at 295 lines of its 300-line bound, so what follows is both the plan, by T195, and the specification, by T198, and neither task wrote a file. Established by T195, by running it, not read: a scan of the last 80 commits of orchestration/state.json, comparing each committed file with formatState of the state as checkState (zod) returns it, which is what plan-state check compares. Every one of the 18 "Tnnn: cost recorded" commits is non-canonical and no other commit is, and each differs in exactly one way: that task's costSource sits last, after notes, where the schema puts it directly after tokens. The mechanism: the store reads the file with JSON.parse and then checkState (src/model/store.ts), so the state the service mutates has keys in schema order; recordCost assigns task.costSource on a task that has no such key (src/model/loop.ts, at service main d9eebd0), so JavaScript appends it at the end; formatState is JSON.stringify(state, null, 2), which preserves that order; and check compares against the zod-parsed state, which restores schema order, so the comparison fails. It comes and goes because the next service write re-reads the file through the schema, restoring order for every task, so the warning stands only between a cost write and the write after it. T188 of this session met it at commit 643bf8a and then reported it as not reproducible at a later commit; that report was wrong in its conclusion, and this is why. task_close's fallback that sets costSource to "reported" (src/model/loop.ts, near line 704) is a second site of the same pattern. Criteria. (1) A cost write leaves the state file in the form plan-state check calls canonical, so no invariant-1 warning follows task_cost. (2) Either both sites that assign costSource onto an existing task are covered — recordCost and task_close's "reported" fallback — or the fix is made once where every write serialises, formatState in src/model/schema.ts, so no field added later can repeat it. (3) Nothing else in the file moves: over this repository's state file, the fixed write's output differs from what the service writes today only by costSource standing in schema order. (4) A test in the service repository fails against the code as it stands: a cost write produces a file that check reports clean, and the task_close reported-tokens path is covered too. (5) plan-state check keeps calling a non-canonical file a warning, not a violation (D109): a violation would turn CI red when the checker's pinned build and the writing build order the schema's fields differently, which is a pin not yet moved after a deploy. (6) One pull request in majodali/project-orchestrator-service; the owner merges it, and that merge deploys. (7) After that deploy this repository's project-orchestrator-service pin moves to the merged commit, and npm run check reports no violations and no warnings when run after a cost write, which is the state the warning showed in. The execute step works from this list. Service pull request #49 (P4-N050) is merged at service main d9eebd0 and touched src/model/render.ts, src/view/treePage.ts, test/loop.test.ts, test/modelRender.test.ts and test/viewPages.test.ts; this fix touches src/model/schema.ts or src/model/loop.ts and a test, so nothing is contended. nodes.outcome: `formatState` writes every object's fields in schema order, the per-site rebuilding in `setCostSource` is gone, and no write can drop or misorder a field the schema carries.
nodes.note: Raised by the reviewer of P4-N054 (T201) as D113. Writes to majodali/project-orchestrator-service, where the owner merges and a merge deploys; a pin move in this repository follows. Repository: that one and this one. Planned by T202, which wrote no file: docs/plans/rebuild.md stands at 295 lines of its 300-line bound, so the criteria are here, pending the ask at T202's close on where this node's plan lives. Confirmed by T202 in a throwaway clone at service main 95b4fb8, by running it. setCostSource (src/model/loop.ts, line 656) destructures sixteen named fields, deletes every key of the task and reassigns them; its callers are recordCost (line 1069) and task_close's "reported" fallback (line 761). A task carrying a field the list does not name loses it: recordCost over a task with an extra key returned the task without it, which is the reviewer's finding. The list matches taskSchema's sixteen fields exactly, order included, so nothing is at risk today. The hazard is real: with one optional field added to taskSchema and setCostSource untouched, the field is dropped by a cost write. Settled by running it: a zod parse restores field order at every level, so nested objects and arrays of objects need no separate handling — a task with reversed keys came back in schema order and a nested docs object with spec before plan came back plan, spec. A field the schema does not declare does not survive a parse, which is what the service already does on read, so nothing changes there. stateSchema.shape is available in zod 4, so the order can also be taken from the shape without validating. Churn: none. formatState of the schema-parsed state is byte-identical to this repository's committed state file, 351,851 bytes, 0 changed. Criteria. (1) formatState takes every object's field order from the schema, at every level, so no list of the schema's field names is kept by hand anywhere in the service. (2) setCostSource's destructure, delete and reassign is gone, and its two callers simply set the field; task.docsOnMerge (src/model/mutations.ts near line 168) and state.highWater (src/model/loop.ts near line 287) keep appending and need no change, because order no longer depends on where a key is assigned. (3) No field the schema declares is dropped by any write: a task carrying every field taskSchema declares keeps them all through a cost write. (4) A test asserts criterion 3 and that each object's serialised key order equals its schema's field order. T202 ran both arms: as the code stands it passes, because the hand list is complete; with one field added to taskSchema alone it fails. With the fix it cannot fail, because both sides come from the schema. (5) A state that does not satisfy the schema is still serialised rather than thrown on, so plan-state import --write over such input writes its import record and reports its findings as it does today; the service's own writes are already protected, since the store refuses a write when checkState reports a violation (src/model/store.ts, line 182). (6) Nothing churns: plan-state render --write over this repository's state file as it stands rewrites it byte for byte. (7) One pull request in majodali/project-orchestrator-service; the owner merges it and that merge deploys; then this repository's project-orchestrator-service pin moves to the merged commit and npm run check reports no violations and no warnings.
